$comment: Native realtime conversation state machine (reducer contract). Input: the 12 unified events of realtime-events.v1 (same keys as its mapCases.expected; itemId may be null and is never used for matching) plus local inputs mute / unmute / tapOrb / playbackDrained / tick{ms} / end / systemInterruption / failed{code} / screenReaderSpeaking{speaking}. Each case replays steps from the initial state; every step locks the statusKey after the input and the ordered effects it emits. Each client implements the same reducer and replays this fixture.

state: 1. State: phase connecting | listening | thinking | speaking | ended; muted; userSpeaking; drainPending; turn {userPending, userText, assistantStarted, assistantDone, assistantText, heldMs, userAfterReply}; idleMs; thinkingMs; earconDone; dormant; reopenAwaitingProgress; screenReaderSpeaking. Initial phase is connecting with everything else false / empty / 0.
statusKey: ended → null; connecting → thinking; listening while muted → muted; otherwise the phase. Muted does not override thinking or speaking.
Inputs with an unknown type change nothing (idleMs included) and emit nothing. After ended every input is ignored.
transitions: ready → listening only from connecting; a later ready (reconnect) changes nothing.

userSpeechStarted → listening, userSpeaking = true, userPending = true, thinkingMs = 0, earconDone = false. While speaking it first emits interruptPlayback (the client stops local playback; the server confirms later). A held assistant reply is released (persisted) before the new utterance starts; if the current reply has started but is not done, the utterance is marked userAfterReply (it belongs to the next turn).
userSpeechStopped → thinking from any live phase, userSpeaking = false, thinkingMs = 0.
assistantAudio → speaking and marks the reply started; assistantTranscript stores the cumulative assistant text and marks the reply started; neither changes anything else.

assistantTurnDone: while speaking stays speaking with drainPending = true, otherwise → listening. playbackDrained → listening only when speaking with drainPending; otherwise it changes nothing (more audio may follow).
interrupted → listening (drainPending cleared, nothing persisted). tapOrb only while speaking: interruptPlayback then → listening; in every other phase it is a no-op (it does not unmute).

goAway / resumable change nothing in this reducer (reconnect and resumption belong to the session layer) but still reset idleMs. The unified error event is non-fatal (realtime-events.v1: the connection close decides fatality): it changes nothing and emits nothing, only resets idleMs; the conversation continues.

planChanged (local; at a turn boundary the host replans off the main thread with currentSessionId = the open session and sends this when the new fingerprint differs from the open session’s, per realtime-session.v1): only in phase listening, not dormant, not userSpeaking and with no turn in progress (no userPending, no assistantStarted) → drainPending = false, turn cleared, phase connecting (statusKey thinking), emit reopen; the host reopens from the new plan and sends ready. Otherwise ignored; the host compares again at the next turn boundary.
persistence: userTranscript stores text in userText. Non-final sets userPending = true (Gemini sends no speech-start signal). Final sets userPending = false and emits persist {role: user, text: trimmed} unless echoUnits(text) is empty (blank or punctuation / separators only, same separator set as voice-conversation.v1 isEcho).

assistantTurnDone text = event.text when it is non-blank after trim, otherwise the latest assistantTranscript (null and "" both fall back). If userPending and the utterance is not userAfterReply, a non-blank reply is held (heldMs = 0); a blank one is not held. Otherwise persist {role: assistant, text: trimmed} immediately; blank text writes nothing.

A held reply is released by the user final (persist user first, then assistant), by tick when heldMs reaches lateUserTranscriptMs (assistant only; a later user final is then persisted on its own), by the next userSpeechStarted, or by the end sequence.

Barge-in: if the userAfterReply utterance goes final before the interrupted reply's assistantTurnDone, the reply is persisted first with its current transcript and that assistantTurnDone writes nothing; if the reply finishes first it is persisted immediately and the utterance (pending flag and text) carries over to the next turn.
After a reply is written the turn is cleared, except the userPending / userText of a userAfterReply utterance.
mute: mute (when not muted): muted = true; if userSpeaking emit sendSilence {ms: muteSilenceMs} first, then setUplink {on: false}. unmute (when muted): muted = false, setUplink {on: true}. Repeated mute / unmute emit nothing.

sessionExpired (local; the host sends it when the transport reports the provider closed the session as expired, Gemini close 1008): while muted and not dormant → persist a held assistant reply, then dormant = true, phase listening, turn cleared, no effects (the call stays open, statusKey muted, idle does not count while muted). Ignored while dormant. unmute while dormant → dormant = false, reopenAwaitingProgress = true, phase connecting, emit reopen then setUplink {on: true}; the host opens a new session from the text history and sends ready when it is up.

Not muted (and not dormant): if reopenAwaitingProgress is false → persist a held assistant reply, turn cleared, userSpeaking = false, drainPending = false, reopenAwaitingProgress = true, phase connecting (statusKey thinking), emit reopen (uplink gating unchanged, it stays on); the host reopens from the text history and sends ready, which goes connecting → listening. If reopenAwaitingProgress is true → showError {code: "sessionExpired"} then end with reason error (no reopen loop). reopenAwaitingProgress is cleared by userTranscript, assistantAudio, assistantTranscript or assistantTurnDone; ready is not progress.

screenReaderSpeaking{speaking} (local; the host sends it when the platform screen reader starts / finishes announcing): screenReaderSpeaking = speaking. Uplink is on only when not muted and the screen reader is not speaking; mute wins. speaking true while not muted → setUplink {on: false}; speaking false while not muted → setUplink {on: true}; while muted both emit nothing and muted / statusKey are unchanged. unmute while the screen reader is speaking clears muted but does not emit setUplink {on: true} (reopen still applies while dormant). Repeated values emit nothing.
timers: tick{ms} is the only clock. There is no periodic tick: after every reduce the host arms one one-shot timer for nextTickMs (cancelling the previous one; none when null); before dispatching any other input, and when that timer fires, it first dispatches tick{ms: monotonic time elapsed since the last tick or since the session became ready}. nextTickMs = min of (lateUserTranscriptMs - heldMs while a reply is held, thinkingEarconMs - thinkingMs while thinking and the earcon has not played, idleEndMs - idleMs while listening, not muted and not userSpeaking), clamped at 0; null when none applies or ended. A tick with ms <= 0 changes nothing, so the host never arms a timer for nextTickMs <= 0 (it would only spin). In this order: held reply heldMs += ms (release at lateUserTranscriptMs); while thinking thinkingMs += ms and the first time it reaches thinkingEarconMs emit earcon (once until the next userSpeechStarted); while listening, not muted and not userSpeaking idleMs += ms and at idleEndMs run the end sequence with reason idle.
Every input other than tick resets idleMs to 0, including goAway, resumable, mute, unmute and no-op tapOrb.

playbackDrained comes from the player's own completion callback when the last queued buffer has played; the host never polls the player. When drainPending turns on and the player has already played everything (so no callback will follow), the host reads the player's state once at that moment and dispatches playbackDrained.
end: end → reason user; systemInterruption and sessionEnded → reason system; local failed {code} (sent by the host when the session stream throws or the connection drops unexpectedly) → emit showError {code} first, then reason error.

End sequence, in order: persist a held assistant reply; for reason user only, writeDraft {text: trimmed userText} when userPending and echoUnits(userText) is non-empty; close; ended {reason}. Then phase = ended, statusKey null. A reply still in progress (not done) is not persisted.
fixture: cases[]: {id, steps: [{input, expected: {statusKey, effects[], nextTickMs}}]}. Effects: persist {role, text}, interruptPlayback, sendSilence {ms}, setUplink {on}, earcon, showError {code}, writeDraft {text}, close, ended {reason}, reopen.
host: Home entry (no conversation yet): on the first assistantAudio, assistant transcript or user transcript event of the session, the host creates the chat and moves to the chat page on the main thread BEFORE it reduces that event and publishes the status, so the home bar never shows speaking (voice-conversation pageReachableStatusKeys.home). Later persist effects write into that conversation in effect order (user before assistant per rules.persistence). Event order does not matter: an assistant reply that arrives before any user transcript still lands on the chat page.
Only the home entry does this. A chat-page entry (draft or existing conversation) never creates through this path and never deletes.
The host tries to create once per session. If creation fails it ends the session with the same error the home cascade first send uses, so the home bar never reaches speaking.

A home session deletes the conversation it created only when all hold: it created it, it persisted nothing into it, and the store still has no message in it (checked and deleted in one transaction, not counted as a user delete). Creation and the handoff are not cancellable halfway: an end during creation still records the created id so the empty check runs. The page holding that conversation is left (only when it is still the current page) before or atomically with the delete, so no send can target a conversation being deleted: iOS removes it from memory and dismisses in one main-actor turn, then deletes in the store; Android leaves the page, then deletes in one transaction. A delete skipped because the store has messages navigates no further.

One user turn, one user message: every inputTranscription fragment of one user turn (until that turn ends at turnComplete; a provider item id, when present, groups fragments the same way) accumulates into one text and is persisted once at the turn boundary. Fragments are never persisted one by one, and two real turns are never merged after the fact.
The event that triggers home creation (often the first user fragment) is not lost: it is reduced only after creation finished, in arrival order, with every later event queued behind it.

Replay: recordings/*.v1.json (gemini-live-home-two-turn with its variants, gemini-live-barge-in) hold real provider server messages; both ends replay them in order through the production mapper, reducer and sink and must produce expectedMessages exactly (order, count, text).
end is synchronous for the UI: active turns false and the bar hides in the same call; audio teardown finishes in the background and never blocks navigation.
